aspects.says: An absent field reads as null from every getter but getMTI, so optional fields are read with a null check.
basis: section:6.1 A Field Holds Text, Bytes or a Message

aspects.says: Binary data is set as bytes; a hex string becomes bytes only if a packager is attached when it is set, so in a client it goes out as text or fails to pack.
basis: section:6.2 Binary Data Goes In as Bytes

aspects.says: A field holds text, bytes or a nested message, and getString gives hex for bytes and null for a nested message.
basis: section:6.1 A Field Holds Text, Bytes or a Message

aspects.says: A clone shares its text and byte components with the original, so a write into a copied array changes both.
basis: section:6.4 A Follow-up Copies the Fields It Lists and Leaves the Original Alone

aspects.says: A follow-up copies the fields it lists with clone(int...) and leaves the original unchanged; copying all and pruning leaks what was forgotten.
basis: section:6.4 A Follow-up Copies the Fields It Lists and Leaves the Original Alone

aspects.says: Setting a new nested ISOMsg replaces the whole field, while dotted paths add to it.
basis: section:6.3 Sub-fields Are a Nested Message That Only a Declaring Packager Can Carry

aspects.says: A receiver whose packager does not declare the sub-fields gets the field as text and null for every sub-field, without an error.
basis: section:6.3.1 The Receiving Side Needs the Declaration Too

aspects.says: setResponseMTI answers a repeat with the response of a first attempt and refuses a response.
basis: section:6.4 A Follow-up Copies the Fields It Lists and Leaves the Original Alone

aspects.says: set(n, byte[]) keeps the caller's array, so a reused buffer changes a request that has not been packed yet.
basis: section:6.2 Binary Data Goes In as Bytes

aspects.says: Sub-fields are a nested ISOMsg set by dotted paths, and only a packager that declares them can pack them.
basis: section:6.3 Sub-fields Are a Nested Message That Only a Declaring Packager Can Carry
